sources.entry: C: _Learning operating system development using Linux kernel and Raspberry Pi_

summary.one_liner: A step-by-step tutorial that teaches building a simple ARM kernel from scratch for Raspberry Pi 3, called RPi OS and largely based on the Linux kernel.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a lesson-based guide to writing an operating system kernel from the ground up. Each lesson explains how a kernel feature is implemented in RPi OS and then shows how the same functionality works in Linux. Lessons cover kernel initialization, processor setup, interrupt handling, a process scheduler, user processes with system calls, and virtual memory management. Each lesson has a matching folder under src containing the OS source as it stood when that lesson was completed. The README's table of contents lists lessons 7 through 11 (signals, file systems, ELF executables, drivers, networking) as not yet written. The README says the guide needs no prior OS development skills.
use_cases: learn operating system development step by step
build a bare-metal kernel for Raspberry Pi 3
study how the Linux kernel implements scheduling and interrupts
follow an OS kernel tutorial with per-lesson code snapshots
understand virtual memory and system calls from scratch
notable: Each lesson includes a snapshot of the source code at lesson completion, so readers can follow the OS's evolution
Every topic is paired with a comparison to how the Linux kernel handles the same feature
Covers bare-metal boot, interrupts, timers, a process scheduler, user mode, and virtual memory
Written as a guided tutorial that requires no prior OS development experience
caveats: Lessons 7 through 11 are listed as to be done, and Linux comparison for lesson 6 is marked in progress
Project is described as still under active development
